---
title: "math-exercise examples"
subtitle: "Interactive answer checking for Quarto"
lang: en
toc: false
---

`math-exercise` turns ordinary Quarto content into browser-based practice
activities. Authors write the task, expected answer, and checking policy in a
short `{math-exercise}` block. During rendering, the extension replaces answer
markers with input fields and connects them to a checker. When a student
selects **Check**, Pyodide and SymPy run locally in the browser; a grading
server is not required.

The extension supports symbolic equivalence, required algebraic forms,
numerical tolerances, vectors and matrices, author-defined Python/SymPy
checkers, and structured answers from JSXGraph. Optional AI feedback can use
the task, the current answer, the checker result, and relevant page context to
give a progressive hint without replacing deterministic answer checking.

It is well suited to self-study notes, formative exercises, interactive
textbooks, laboratory instructions, and visual mathematical exploration on a
static Quarto website. It is not intended as a secure high-stakes examination
system: expected answers and checker code are delivered to the student's
browser.

Choose a page below to try common exercise types and see the corresponding
Quarto source. Every source example is collapsed until you choose **Show
source**.

::: {.callout-tip title="Trying the exercises"}
Type in the empty answer fields and select **Check**. Some exercises are hidden
under a clickable heading. For mathematical input, use forms such as `x^2`,
`2*x`, `sqrt(2)`, `sin(x)`, and `pi`; **Input help** provides a complete
reference. Graphical exercises explain directly which points or curves to move.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
All answer checking runs locally in the browser through SymPy and Pyodide.
AI-generated progressive feedback is optional and works with OpenAI-compatible
providers configured by the user.
:::
